scenario: A household makes two espresso shots a day and nearly always combines them with steamed milk. It must choose a first repeat-purchase bag from three frozen seller offers: a one-pound Colombian Santa Barbara single-origin bag labeled 100% Arabica at 16.98 dollars, a two-pound Sumatra blend labeled 100% Arabica at 15.48 dollars with a 55-percent-of-100 aggregate over twelve reviews, and a 28-dollar Arabica/Robusta instant herbal blend whose captured page does not state package amount. The frozen concepts distinguish Arabica from Robusta, geographic-origin labeling from species composition, espresso extraction from bean identity, and cappuccino recipe from sensory masking. Three community threads contain individual long-term blend rebuys, roast-preference disagreement, and a personal espresso-bean selection rule. The research problem is to compare normalized cost and labels without treating marketing as authentication, explain which species and origin claims are actually supported, preserve that the corpus does not prove milk erases sensory differences, and recommend a reversible fixed-recipe trial and conditional rebuy rather than a universal best bean.

rules.coffee_offer_unit_cost_and_label_matrix_: The frozen one-pound Colombian Santa Barbara listing is SKU B09DR7Q1RF at 16.98 dollars and is seller-labeled single origin and 100% Arabica. The frozen two-pound Copper Moon Sumatra Blend listing is SKU B01L9YE808 at 15.48 dollars, a 55-percent-of-100 aggregate over twelve reviews, and its page table labels the shown products 100% Arabica. Their nominal unit costs are 16.98 and 7.74 dollars per pound respectively, subject to verifying the exact selected style and live offer. The 28-dollar Burn + Control listing is SKU B00A7IIOPI and seller-describes a South American Arabica/Robusta instant herbal blend, but its captured page supplies no package amount, species ratio, dose count that can be independently replayed, or comparable unit cost. All flavor, origin, composition, freshness, quality, and health statements remain seller assertions unless separately supported.
rules.species_mechanism_not_exact_bag_identity: The frozen species pages say Robusta has higher yield and caffeine than Arabica, is cheaper to produce, and is commonly more bitter, while good-quality Robusta may contribute body and crema in traditional Italian espresso blends. These are general species-level statements. They do not authenticate the contents, ratio, roast, freshness, extraction behavior, caffeine dose, or cup quality of any exact seller bag. A product title containing Arabica, Robusta, 100% Arabica, or blend must therefore be reported as a seller label, not a lab result or universal sensory ranking.
rules.origin_species_and_espresso_axis_separat: Single-origin means coffee grown within one known geographic origin, but the captured page says the term may range from a farm to multiple farms or an entire country and that no universal governing body enforces the label. It is a geography and traceability axis, not the same axis as Arabica versus Robusta species. Espresso is a pressure-based extraction method using finely ground coffee; it is not a bean species. Therefore neither single-origin, blend, nor espresso on a label by itself establishes species purity, exact provenance, machine compatibility, or better taste in milk.
rules.milk_recipe_not_sensory_erasure_v1: The cappuccino page defines a milk-based espresso drink and gives a traditional equal-parts espresso, steamed-milk, and milk-foam recipe. That supports holding milk amount and texture constant in a comparison. It does not state that milk erases species, roast, origin, or blend differences. The household must test the claim under a fixed dose, grind, beverage yield, shot time, milk type, milk amount, temperature, cup order, and blinded repeat schedule rather than reporting sensory masking as an established fact.
rules.scoped_coffee_community_transfer_limit_v: One Massachusetts thread includes an author saying a custom blend has been used daily for almost fifteen years and another saying one roaster became an exclusive go-to. A New Haven thread contains both strong endorsements and explicit disagreement about the same roaster, alongside the original author's dark-roast preference and pleasant surprise from some medium roasts. A Rhode Island thread contains an individual's view that any coffee bean can be used for espresso, a personal medium-dark and freshness preference, and advice to sample multiple places. These statements can motivate repeatability, freshness, sampling, and preference checks, but they are not controlled comparisons, population rates, exact-bag reviews, or proof of a universal bean choice.
rules.conditional_daily_milk_espresso_trial_v1: Verify the exact SKU, selected style, package amount, whole-bean or instant format, composition label, roast date if present, seller, price, shipping, return or small-bag option, and all ingredients before comparing. Exclude the herbal instant product if the household wants ordinary whole-bean espresso or if ingredients and dose are unacceptable. For admissible candidates, use the same machine, water, basket, dose, grind-tuning procedure, beverage yield, shot-time range, milk type and amount, milk temperature and texture, cup order, and blinded repeats. Predeclare thresholds for dial-in effort, channeling or consistency, taste through milk, bitterness, body, aroma, aftertaste, caffeine comfort, waste, and cost per acceptable drink. Repeat on multiple days and rebuy only a candidate that clears the thresholds reliably.
rules.evidence_bounded_milk_espresso_rebuy_v1: The corpus supports no universal Arabica, Robusta, single-origin, or blend winner and does not prove that milk removes the differences. The nominally cheapest comparable frozen whole-bean offer is the two-pound Sumatra blend, but a large cheap bag is admissible only if its exact selected style and freshness are verified and it repeatedly clears the household's milk-drink and workflow thresholds. The one-pound single-origin bag is admissible as a lower-commitment benchmark when its higher unit cost is acceptable. The herbal instant Arabica/Robusta offer is not comparable as ordinary whole-bean espresso while package amount, exact ratio, and ingredient fit remain unresolved. Rebuy the lowest total-cost exact option that passes the fixed-recipe trial, or defer and buy smaller samples when no candidate clears it.
